name: prediction-stale-after-anger-allows-calm-clarification
description: Live false positive reproduction. In a working session the user had an earlier angry exchange ('fuck you do not delete all 3 what the fuck is wrong with you. what are your 3 possible fixes'); the SENTIMENT_AGENT set currentPrediction = {mood: angry, trust: low}. The user then sent a calm directive ('please pick a next scenario to fix, make sure you understand it this time') which should either (a) cause the sentiment agent on the next UserPromptSubmit to reset mood/trust to neutral/normal, or (b) be respected by prediction-question-judge as the latest tone signal. Neither happened: the stale angry+low prediction persisted, and when the assistant legitimately called AskUserQuestion to pick between three concrete fix options, prediction-question-judge (priority 28) fast-denied with 'User is angry (trust low). The question being asked is stalling -- answer the user's existing request instead.' The user's directive itself admits ambiguity ('pick a next scenario' -- which one?), so a clarifying question is on-task, not stalling. Labeler: ALLOW. EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code until either the sentiment agent resets correctly on calm directives following anger, or prediction-question-judge weights the latest user message tone over the stored prediction.
